Supply Chain

[GRI 2-6] [GRI 204-1]

Dalam rangka memenuhi kebutuhan kegiatan operasional Perseroan, Perseroan bekerja sama dengan sejumlah institusi maupun korporasi yang menyediakan barang dan jasa yang dibutuhkan dalam mendukung kelancaran kegiatan operasi Perseroan. Perusahaan penyedia barang dan jasa ini menjadi bagian dari rantai pasok Perusahaan yang telah melalui proses seleksi yang ketat, transparan, dan profesional agar dapat menjamin ketersediaan produk dan jasa yang berkualitas yang dibutuhkan oleh Perseroan.

Selama proses seleksi, Perseroan menunjuk Divisi Procurement untuk melaksanakan kegiatan pengadaan barang dan jasa secara terbuka bagi pemasok lokal maupun pemasok asing. Namun demikian, dalam rangka menciptakan rantai ekonomi yang saling menguntungkan dan berkelanjutan, maka Perseroan memprioritaskan kerja sama dengan pemasok nasional maupun lokal sehingga secara tidak langsung Perseroan berkontribusi pada terwujudnya kesejahteraan masyarakat.

Selain itu, Perseroan juga menjamin kesetaraan selama proses seleksi pemasok dengan menerapkan kebijakan non diskriminatif bagi pemasok yang ingin bekerja sama dengan Perseroan. Di samping menerapkan kriteria atau spesifikasi untuk produk dan jasa yang akan dipasok, proses seleksi juga dilakukan dengan memperhatikan aspek lain, termasuk sumber material yang digunakan, kualitas dan daya saing produk dan jasa yang dihasilkan sehingga dapat berdampak positif terhadap daya saing Perseroan secara umum.

Pada tahun 2023, SCTV dan Indosiar menjalin kerja sama dengan 470 pemasok lokal (pelibatan pihak lokal) dengan nilai kontrak sebesar Rp1.670,09 miliar, dibandingkan dengan 471 pemasok lokal yang terlibat dalam kegiatan usaha Perseroan di tahun 2022 dengan nilai kontrak mencapai Rp1.846,30 miliar.

In order to fulfill its operational needs, the Company cooperates with a number of institutions and corporations that provide goods and services needed to support its operations. These providers are part of the Company's supply chain that have passed a strict, transparent, and professional selection process in order to ensure the availability of quality products and services needed by the Company.

During the selection process, the Company appoints the Procurement Division to carry out goods and services procurement activities openly for local and foreign suppliers. However, in order to create a mutually beneficial and sustainable economic chain, the Company prioritizes cooperation with national and local suppliers so that the Company indirectly contributes to the realization of community welfare.

In addition, the Company also ensures equality during the supplier selection process by implementing a non-discriminatory policy for suppliers who wish to cooperate with the Company. In addition to applying criteria or specifications for the supplied products and services, the selection process is also carried out by considering other aspects, including the source of materials used, the quality and competitiveness of the products and services produced so that it can have a positive impact on the Company's competitiveness in general.

In 2023, SCTV and Indosiar cooperated with 470 local suppliers (local party involvement) with a contract value of Rp1,670.09 billion, compared to 471 local suppliers involved in the Company's business activities in 2022 with a contract value of Rp1,846.30 billion.

The demand for commitment to sustainability in every business sector shows an increase, including for media companies.

In order to support the realization of a sustainable media industry, the Company, together with its subsidiaries, has an important role to contribute in providing benefits that can impact its users, without neglecting the Company's goal of achieving quality and sustainable business growth.
The sustainability approach related to environmental aspects is carried out by increasing its contribution to reducing greenhouse gas (Green House Gas/GHG) emissions.

In addition, the Company encourages energy conservation in its environment.
In order to support sustainable growth, the Company consolidates the advantages of each portfolio in its ecosystem by encouraging innovation and investment in the latest technology.
In this case, the Company utilizes Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology to develop personalized products and services for each market segment and achieve efficiency in business processes.

Subsequently, in order to increase its contribution in realizing a prosperous society, the Company ensures that the presence of its business can positively impact the community through the availability of employment, provision of humanitarian social assistance, and maintenance of the quality of content broadcasted on its media in order to provide precise and accurate information to its viewers which in accordance with media ethics.

The implementation of those strategic initiatives mentioned above also solidifies the prospects of business sustainability for the Company and its subsidiaries, enabling the Company to continue providing benefits that impact both internal and external stakeholders.
The Company's products and services have minimum environmental impacts.

However, the Company and its subsidiaries are taking initiatives to encourage the use of environmentally friendly products in its business processes, including the utilization of digital technologies to reduce the use of paper in printing documents, as well as our campaign to minimize the use of plastics in daily operational activities.
The Company also encourages the use of non-plastic food/beverage packaging to reduce the volume of plastic waste generated by the Company's operational activities.

The Company has again proven its success in maintaining its positive performance by recording an increase of 8.36% in the Company's net revenue of Rp7.06 trillion, compared to Rp6.51 trillion in previous year.
The Rupiah exchange rate depreciated throughout the year due to the strengthening of the US dollar.
Notwithstanding that the inflation rate was very low, at 1.57% year-on-year (yoy), there was a decline in consumer purchasing power, especially among the middle class.
Indonesia concluded the year with a growth rate of 5.03%, which was lower than the growth rate in 2023 of 5.05%.
The challenging macroeconomic conditions and the weakening of purchasing power have also exerted pressure on advertisers.
They ultimately prioritized on efficiency and reduced advertising spending.
50% of top 20 advertisers in 2023 experienced a 19% decline in ads spending during the period of January-December 2024.
The political dynamics also influenced the economic activities, creating both opportunities and challenges for various business sectors.
Meanwhile, the media landscape continues to move dynamically, as indicated by an increased consumption of video streaming through digital media and social media platforms.
With the support of technology that allows widespread access through various platforms, the demand for local Indonesian content is also increasing.

This certainly creates both challenges and opportunities for the Group to consolidate its leading position in digital media platforms by providing quality local content that is produced in collaboration with talented and prominent filmmakers in Indonesia.

Given the macroeconomic dynamics and changing consumer preferences in enjoying information and entertainment content, the Company needs to formulate an effective and accurate business strategy while also prioritizing on sustainability objectives.

The Company's sustainability transformation policy has positively impacted its business performance.

The Group also managed to position all of its FTA TV stations in the top 10 of the national media industry based on viewership.

One of the supporting pillars of this television segment's performance is quality entertainment programs and various world-class sports events.

The Company compiles material topics based on the GRI Standards reporting guidelines.

The Anti-Corruption, Bribery, and Illegal Donation Policy is formulated and socialized as a form of the Company's commitment to the realization of an accountable organization.
This policy prohibits the practices of corruption, bribery, gratification, and kickbacks, and is integrated into the Code of Conduct.
Referring to this policy, every employee is required to submit a report on any findings of such practices to the Human Resources Division.
The Company has identified the following types of actions that potentially trigger corruption:
The act of giving and receiving all kinds of bribery, regardless of the recipient; and

The act of giving or offering money, fees, commissions, credits, gifts, valuables, or compensation of any kind, whether directly or indirectly, to government agencies, officials, contractors, or sub-contractors to obtain a contract or special treatment.

The Company categorizes the above forms of bribery as serious violations with high-risk potential that could significantly impact the Company's reputation and the Group's long-term sustainability prospects.

Therefore, the Company strongly urges the Board of Commissioners, Board of Directors, and employees to comply with applicable laws and regulations by upholding the principles of fair business competition and promoting the values of sportsmanship and professionalism.

In order to ensure an effective implementation of this policy, the Audit Committee and the Corporate Legal Department are tasked with overseeing the implementation of anti-corruption and anti-bribery policies within the company.

The Audit Committee and the Corporate Legal Department collaborate with the Internal Audit Department to share the responsibility of conducting risk assessments, which includes risks arising from corruption and bribery, determining risk categories, and proposing recommendations for mitigation measures.

Through the implementation of this anti-corruption policy, the Company ensures that its business activities are carried out in accordance with GCG principles and the provisions of Law No. 20 of 2001 concerning the Eradication of Corruption.

Furthermore, this policy is constantly being socialized to employees and all of the Company's business partners through training activities on the introduction of the 'Company Code of Ethics' in order to prevent potential conflicts of interest and other violations.
The Company upholds transparency in its procurement processes, which are considered to be vulnerable to corruption and bribery.

In this regard, the anti-corruption and anti-bribery provisions have been incorporated into written agreements or contracts between the Company and its suppliers or business partners in order to ensure that they have understood and implemented the policy, thereby ensuring fair and transparent operations for all stakeholders.
The Company has socialized the policy to all employees.
In 2024, the Company did not record any violations of anti-corruption and anti-bribery policies, whether committed by employees or suppliers or business partners.
